candidates.title: Prepare a recovery checklist for failed agent runs

demandEvidence.chore: Developers need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and handle idempotency for agents.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency

experimentPlan.output: A human-reviewed recovery worksheet for one failed agent run, listing saved state, safe retry point, and duplicate-action risks.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a failed-run example for review.
steps: Extract the last known checkpoint from supplied notes.
Flag actions that may repeat if retried.
Draft a recovery checklist and ask a person to approve each action.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On two synthetic cases, verify every listed action matches the supplied log and that uncertain side effects are flagged for human review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A developer must define safe checkpoints, idempotency rules, and authorize recovery; the worksheet must never restart an agent or perform side effects.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents agent checkpoint recovery or idempotency validation.
The discussion does not specify agent type, recurrence, fields, or recovery policy.

ease.reason: The comment identifies recovery concepts, but no supplied implementation source supports checkpoint or idempotency handling.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: agent development consultancies may pay for safer recovery reviews; this comment shows a problem, not buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic worksheet is testable in four weeks, but the needed agent logs and safe retry rules are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed worksheet is mainly human review; no source supports automated recovery decisions or execution.

evidence.reason: The comment names checkpointers, recovery logic, and idempotency, but gives no example or evidence of repeated demand.

candidates.reason: Concrete concepts support a narrow manual-review prototype, but there is no reference for its core recovery mechanics and the experiment remains below threshold.

candidates.title: Send daily alerts for new jobs at target companies

demandEvidence.chore: Track hiring at target companies and send an alert when new job postings appear.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Workflow: Schedule Trigger (daily) → Apify node (“Run an Actor and get dataset”) → IF item count > 0 → Slack.

experimentPlan.output: A daily test digest of new job listings from a small operator-selected set of target companies.
inputs: Synthetic listing rows with title, location, and URL
experimentPlan.trigger: A daily scheduled run checks a configured test listing source.
steps: Collect the available listing rows from an authorized test source.
Compare rows with the previous test run.
Use the documented Summarize node to count or count unique values when checking a batch.
Format new rows as a digest with title, location, and URL.
Ask a person to review results before any real alert is sent.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Across two supplied test batches, the digest includes each new row once and preserves its title, location, and URL; a person checks missed or repeated items.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must authorize source access, choose target companies, confirm listing relevance, and approve live alerts; the supplied reference does not document job scraping or Slack delivery.
unverified: The n8n reference documents count and count-unique aggregation only, not scheduling, scraping, deduplication, or Slack delivery.
The author discloses building the named Apify actors; their availability, accuracy, and external runtime are not independently established here.

ease.reason: The source lays out a daily trigger, new-item condition, and alert fields; the Summarize reference supports counts only, not source access or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: recruiting consultancies may pay for target-company monitoring; this post describes one maker’s workflow, not buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A supplied-row experiment is bounded and the source describes a daily flow; the reference supports aggregation only, leaving live collection and delivery unverified.

autonomy.reason: The source describes repeated daily checks and new-item alerts; a person must verify relevance, while the reference does not validate scraping or sending.

evidence.reason: The spans describe one author’s daily job tracking flow and alert fields; broader demand and independent use are not established.

candidates.reason: A specific daily alert chore and relevant limited aggregation reference support a scoped test, but the provisional mean is 5.4 and below threshold.

steps.message: Assessed all eight assigned discussions. Two concrete chores received scoped provisional assessments; six were excluded for missing task detail or a one-off incident. Neither scored experiment reaches the threshold, so no post is proposed.
